nodes.question: What types of carnivores are present in the region's wildlife?
nodes.answer: The carnivores present include spotted hyenas, leopards, and lions.
nodes.paragraph: The local fauna boasts a diverse array of animals. Notable her-bivores found in the area encompass the African buffalo (Syncerus caffer ), waterbuck ( Kobus ellipsiprymnus ), plains zebra ( Equus quagga ), blue wildebeest ( Connochaetes taurinus ), eland ( Taurotragus oryx ), and impala ( Aepyceros melampus melampus ). The region S wildlife also features a variety of carnivores, including spotted hyenas ( Crocuta crocuta ), leopards ( Panthera pardus ), and lions ( Panthera leo), among other species. All the property holders are obliged to conduct anti-poaching on their properties. Tro-phy hunting and other natural resource related activities like shing and photography are the income generating activ- ities in the conservancy. The communities that boarder the conservancy are den- sely populated (11 80 people/km 2) (ZimStat, 2012 ). This study was carried out in villages at Chibuwe, Chechecheand Birchenough. The area is located in a semiarid region ve (V) in Masvingo Province which receives very little annual rainfall of 474 540 mm per annum. The area has poor-quality soils which are not suitable for agriculture.

The relative paucity of information on the status of small carnivores in Southeast Asia, coupled with the regions rapid deforestation, amplifies the urgency of assessing their conservation status (Chiaverini et al. 2022; Macdonald et al. 2020). Southeast Asia supports the largest number of sympatric felids of any region in the world (Macdonald and Loveridge 2010). Of these, tigers and leopards have been the main focus of past conservation efforts and economic investments (Brodie 2009; Mac- donald et al. 2015), and clouded leopards have recently gained attention (Macdonald et al. 2018, 2019). nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is the significance of small mammals in food chains?
nodes.answer: Small mammals play a key role in food chains as they are an important food source for various predators, including birds of prey and small carnivores.
nodes.paragraph: 2015). While the conservation threats faced by large mammals are known to most people, as these are known as flagship species and are the focus of conservation strategies and campaigns by major conservation and environmental organizations (e.g., giant panda, whales, wolf, wildcat, European otter), threats to small mammals are often less well known (exempting perhaps bats or dormice) and therefore often go unnoticed. In addition, most small mammals are harder to observe or even to detect and their natural history is relatively unknown. Nevertheless, they are an integral part of biodiversity and play a key role in ecosystems, as they are an important part in food chains. nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do small mammals contribute to the ecological balance?
nodes.answer: Small mammals play an important ecological role and monitoring them is crucial in understanding the impacts of global biodiversity loss on ecosystem functions.
nodes.paragraph: These are usually based on direct observations, hunting bags, or from a variety of sources such as trapping, individuals found dead, road kill, predation remains, owl pellets in collections, and museum records. Despite the comprehensive knowledge of faunistic and natural history, substantial knowledge gaps exist concerning several small mammal species. Closing these gaps is one of the major interests of biodiversity research and conservation. It also has implications for pest management, since some microtine rodents are still considered a pest to agriculture in some regions, in particular at the peak of their population cycles (Jacob et al. 2020). There are also public health concerns that require knowledge about the distribution of the spe- cies that might carry human pathogenic viruses (e.g., hanta or cowpox virus) or bacteria (e.g., Leptospira; Essbauer et al. 2010). But several vole species are also known to be intermediate hosts of the zoonotic tapeworm Echinococcus multilocularis (Mart nek et al. 1998; Woolsey et al 2015a, b). Given their ecological role, small mammal monitoring is important in a changing world that faces dramatic global biodiversity loss with substantial impact on the function of ecosystems.
